note: Source differences, selected readings and their explanations are recorded below.

adjudicated.ruling: The approved Benziger printing prints fílii Israël (p. 387), the nominative plural subject of possent. The digital source prints the vocative singular fili.
The selected accentuation follows the approved Benziger printing. The pinned digital reading is recorded exactly; the word is the same.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the approved 1962 Benziger printing sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Ordo Missae of Pallottinum, Poznań 1963, which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
The approved Benziger printing's punctuation is retained. The difference marks phrasing and does not change the words.
